password.description:
The existing account's password, or the one being chosen for a new
account. Which it is depends on `has_account`.

duplicate.description:
**True when this exact event had already arrived.** Still a `202`: the
provider did nothing wrong, and answering an error would make them retry
something that is already done.

event_id.description: The provider's id, echoed so a caller can correlate.

token.description: Ready to use — accepting signs you in.

expense.description: The cost. `5100` in every shipped chart.

payable.description: What is owed to people until it is paid. `2200`.

withheld.description: What is held on their behalf. `2210`.

output_vat.description: Credited by tax charged and owed to ZATCA. Defaults to 2100.

receivable.description: Debited by what customers owe. Defaults to 1100.

revenue.description: Credited by what was earned, excluding tax. Defaults to 4000.

branch.description:
Only when this business wants its invoices distinct per branch. Absent,
the unit is the whole business.

environment.description:
`sandbox`, `simulation` or `production` — whichever portal the OTP was
generated in.

otp.description:
**The six digits the taxpayer generates in the Fatoora portal.** Valid
for about an hour, used once, and never stored here.

checks_expected.description: How many sample documents the worker will submit.

compliance.description:
The certificate the OTP bought. It can sign the compliance samples and
nothing else.

state.description:
`checking`: the worker now submits the samples and asks for the
production certificate. Watch `GET /v1/tax_sa/zatca/onboarding`.

AddressBody.description: A Saudi national address, which is a shape rather than free text.

additional.description: The four-digit secondary number, where the address has one.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. `SA` for a business registered here.

AgedCustomerView.description: One customer's debt, split by how late it is.

customer.description: A name to show: the one the most recent invoice in this group froze.

identified.description:
Whether `key` is a customer id.

`false` means these invoices were grouped by the name they froze, so two
spellings of one buyer are two rows. Record them in `crm` and reference
them to merge.

key.description:
What this row is grouped under: a customer id, or the frozen name when
the invoices named no record.

oldest_due.description:
The due date of the oldest unpaid invoice. What a collections call opens
with.

total.description: Every bucket together, in this currency.

AmendBookable.description: The same fields without the id, which cannot change.

oneOf.description: See `NewBookable::rate`. Absent withdraws a published price.

AmendCustomerRecord.description: The same fields without the id, which cannot change.

Amount.description:
An amount, as a client sends it — and as a setting made of one answers it
back, so what a screen reads is what it sends.

Minor units and an explicit currency — never a decimal string, and never a
float. A client that sends `10.50` has already lost the argument about how
many decimal places the currency has.

minor.description: The amount in the currency's smallest unit. 1050 is 10.50 SAR.

unit.description: The resource picked out of the pool this line booked.

AuditView.description: One thing that was done, by whom, and when.

actor.description: Who did it. Null for the system, and for somebody since erased.

actor_handle.description:
The actor's login, where you may see it: on a tenant's trail and your
own, only when they are, or were, a member of the tenant the entry
concerns — so staff who never were appear by id alone. Null for an
actor with no password login, such as an API key.

detail.description: The particulars, shaped by `action`. A suspension's `reason` is here.

on_behalf_of.description: Whose behalf the actor acted on, when staff acted as somebody.

subject_type.description:
What it was done to — `tenant`, `identity`, `api_key`, `effect`, … —
and which one.

tenant.description:
The company it concerns. Null for one about a person or the platform
alone.

held.description:
Settled amounts less the fees already booked. **This is what the
clearing account should say**, and a disagreement is worth chasing.

wage.description: The wage the award was computed on, so the figure can be checked.

documents.description:
Documents with a tax point in this period. Invoices and credit notes on
the output side; bills on the input side.

BarView.description: One resource a customer must not be booked with.

name.description: What it is called now, when it is still declared.

why.description:
**Staff only.** Written by one member of staff about a customer, and
never repeated back in the refusal a booking gets — a reader that shows
this on a customer-facing screen is a bug in that reader.

BeginSecondFactor.description: What starting an enrolment costs an account whose factor somebody reset.

link.description:
The token from the enrolment email, **sent in the body rather than the
path** for the reason a reset token is: a path lands in access logs,
browser history and the `Referer` of every asset the page loads.

Needed only by an account somebody else's reset left link-only. Send
`{}` otherwise.

unread.description: **The number on the badge**, for the whole inbox — not for this page.

position.description:
Where it landed in the log. A client that wants to read its own write
back passes this as `?consistent_after=`.

Billed.description: The invoice a booking was billed on.

deducted.description: The prepayment invoice it deducted, when a deposit had been paid.

invoice.description: The invoice's id — `bk-<reservation>`, so asking again finds it.

raised.description:
**Whether this call raised it**, or found it already raised. A retry,
or the worker reading a read model that had not yet caught up, answers
the same invoice and `false`.

on_completion.description:
**Raise the invoice the moment a booking is completed.** Off until the
business turns it on: the desk can always bill on demand, and a salon
that adds things at the till wants to. The invoice deducts the deposit's
prepayment invoice, so the customer is charged only the rest.

subject.description: Only on email. Empty everywhere else.

branch.description: Which branch it is at. Absent in a single-branch business.

employee.description: Which member of staff this is, when the business keeps staff records.

oneOf.description: The published price, before tax, when there is one.

BookedResource.description: A resource a line takes, and how much of it.

quantity.description: Defaults to one, which is what a stylist and a chair are.

position.description:
The log position this landed at. Pass it to a read as
`?consistent_after=` to see it in the diary.

closed_before.description:
**The first instant still open.** Everything strictly before it is final
and no entry may be dated into it — not a journal entry, not an invoice's
tax point, not a credit note's.

Closing January is `2026-02-01T00:00:00Z`. Exclusive, like the VAT
return's `until`, because "closed through 31 January" is a comparison
somebody gets wrong by exactly one day.

`null` on a tenant that has never closed a period, and the way to reopen
everything.

country.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, two letters. Printed on every document this branch
issues, which is why it is checked rather than stored as typed.

closed_at.description:
Set when it stopped trading. **It keeps everything it traded**, so a
report over last year still names it.

below_zero.description: The shelves here below zero, by product.

branch.description: Absent on the shelves of a business that sends no `X-Branch`.

expired.description: Open lots dated before `today`, still on the shelf.

expiring.description:
Open lots dated from `today` to `expiring_through`. A lot dated today is
still good today, so it is here and not in `expired`.

products.description:
How many products have a shelf here, whatever is on it: the rows
`GET /v1/inventory/stock?branch=` lists.

value.description:
What the shelves here are carried at, one amount per currency: the
`value`s `GET /v1/inventory/stock?branch=` lists, added up — the debt
of a shelf below zero already off it.

configured.description: Whether a person chose these, or they are what shipped. Read-only.

sms.description: **Segments, not messages.** An Arabic message over 70 characters is two.

CalendarView.description:
An IANA timezone, by name. Daylight saving, where the zone has it, is the
zone's business and not a setting.

oneOf.description:
**What is still owed** against the counts. Absent on a card that has
never earned, which has no currency to say it in.

lifetime.description:
Every count ever earned. **Never decreases**, and it is what a rank is
read from: spending points does not cost a rank.

Cash.description:
An amount on the way out. `erp_web::Amount` is the way in and is
deserialize-only, which is the right asymmetry: a client sends what it
believes and reads back what the books say.

minor.description: The amount in the currency's smallest unit. `1050` is 10.50 SAR.

deprecated.description: Set when the module is no longer offered. A picker should hide it.

requires_any.description: What this module needs **at least one** of. Empty for most.

request_id.description: ZATCA's `requestID`. The production request quotes the compliance one.

stage.description:
`compliance` for what an OTP buys, `production` for what a passed
compliance check buys.

serial.description: Its serial number, in hex. What ZATCA's support desk asks for.

subject.description: The certificate's subject, as one line.

current.description:
The password being replaced. Asked for because a session left open on a
shared machine is not proof of anything.

ChargedLine.description: What a line came to, as it was priced.

band.description: The band that applied, or absent for the base rate.

net.description: **What is charged, before tax.** `gross` less every allowance.

uplift.description: What the band did, in basis points. `2500` is a quarter more.

opened_codes.description:
**Which ones**, in the order the chart lists them.

The counts alone are not something a person can check, and this shape is
also what a *preview* answers — the same field names, because the
preview is the same run against a transaction that is rolled back.

skipped.description: Accounts that were already there. Installing twice is not an error.

preview.description:
Enough to show the chart before installing it, which is the
"modify before installing" story's first half — after installing, every
account is renameable and closeable.

holders.description:
**Everyone who now holds this claim**, not just the person named.

A grant at a leaf escalates every ancestor. A screen that showed only
the person being granted would hide the thing somebody has to see.

propagates.description:
Whether it travels up the reporting line. `false` when the claim is on
the segregation-of-duties list, whatever was asked for.

phone.description: The number as it was understood, so a caller can show it back.

code.description: The six digits from the text.

configured.description:
`false` when nothing has been configured and these are the shipped
defaults — so a settings screen can say "using the standard chart"
rather than implying somebody chose this.

base.description: What the contribution was computed on, **after the ceiling**.

employer.description: Paid by the business on top of it.

total.description: Both together, which is what reaches the authority.

kind.description: `note` — internal, `said` — sent to the customer, `heard` — they replied.

who.description: The identity that wrote it. Absent on `heard`.

code.description:
**The six digits from an authenticator app, or a recovery code.**

Only needed by an account that has enrolled a second factor. Sending one
that has not is harmless and is ignored, so a client may always ask for
it rather than first discovering which accounts are enrolled — which
would be an enumeration oracle.

Omitting it for an account that needs one answers `401` with code
`auth.second_factor_required`, which is the signal to ask and retry.

handle.description: The email address the account was registered with.

CreditNoteView.description: A credit note as a list shows it.

compliance_documents.description: How many sample documents the compliance checks will want afterwards.

csr.description:
**The certificate request, base64** — what goes in the `csr` field of
ZATCA's `POST /compliance`, with the OTP in an `OTP` header.

next.description: What to do with what comes back.

position.description:
The log position this landed at. Pass it to a read as
`?consistent_after=` to see it in a list.

vat_number.description: Fifteen digits, beginning and ending with 3.

DeadLetterView.description:
One dead letter, on either plane's list — the tenant's here, the control
plane's under `/v1/platform/effects/dead`.

deferred.description: Where what is owed to customers is held. `2400` in every shipped chart.

revenue.description: Where it lands as it is earned. `4000`.

DepositDue.description: What the customer has to pay, and the charge to pay it against.

amount.description: Minor units, tax included. Worked out here; the caller sends no amount.

due_by.description:
**When the slot stops being held.** Nothing is reserved for somebody who
has not paid by then.

net.description:
What it comes to before tax, and the tax on it, so a page can show the
customer the breakdown it is about to charge them.

pay_at.description:
**Where the customer goes to pay**, when a lender hosts the page. `null`
until the worker has opened the checkout — a tick, not a request — and
always `null` for a card, which is paid in the browser.

payment.description:
**The charge to pay.** For a card, give this to the gateway's form as its
own id — Moyasar's `given_id` — so what the customer pays is this charge
and not one the browser chose. For a lender, poll `GET` on this same
path until `pay_at` names the page to send them to.

provider.description: Which provider it is paid through.

DepositPolicy.description: Whether keeping a deposit is a sale.

supply.description:
**The tax is not what this decides.** A deposit is billed by a
prepayment invoice when the money arrives, so the VAT was declared then
and is not reversed when the money is kept.

What it decides is whether the money the business kept is service
revenue or a line of its own — which is what lets them say, a year
later, how much of their income was selling something and how much was
people not turning up. Defaults to `true`, which is what the document
already says.

DepositRequest.description: How the customer wants to pay. **Optional, and empty is a card.**

email.description:
**Required by a lender**, which scores the buyer before it will lend.
Never shown to staff, and never used to match a customer record.

phone.description:
E.164, or something a person would write that reads as one. Falls back
to the number the booking was made with. Required by a lender, which
sends its one-time code there.

provider.description:
`moyasar` (the default), `tabby` or `tamara`. Only one this business has
configured; anything else is refused by name.

oneOf.description:
**Where the customer lands when the lender is done with them.** Required
by a lender; each must be on an origin this business has allowed.

DepositStatus.description: Where a booking's deposit has got to.

due_by.description: When the hold lapses, while it is still a hold.

paid.description: Whether the money is real and the slot is theirs.

pay_at.description:
Where to send the customer, while there is somewhere. See
[`DepositDue::pay_at`].

stage.description:
`requested` (asked for, nothing at the gateway yet), `pending` (at the
gateway, waiting on the customer or a capture), `settled`, `failed`.

DisableSecondFactor.description: What turning a second factor off costs: proof that you hold it.

code.description:
A code from the app, or one of the recovery codes. Absent only when
there is nothing enrolled to prove — abandoning an enrolment that was
started and never confirmed.

DocumentLimitView.description: The document limit, as the owner reads and writes it.

oneOf.description:
`null`, or absent, is no limit — how every tenant starts, and how an
owner removes one.

icv.description:
Where it sits in the hash chain. Absent on a document issued before the
business registered, which has no place in it.

kind.description:
`standard` — cleared before the buyer gets it — or `simplified`,
reported within 24 hours.

number.description: The statutory number, which is the document's identity.

qr.description:
The base64 TLV block that goes on the printed document. Five fields
before the document is signed, nine after — the last four are the stamp.

remarks.description: Warnings on an accepted document, errors on a refused one.

source.description: The invoice it was built from.

record_name.description: Where to publish the proof: a DNS `TXT` record at this name…

verification_token.description:
**The same token every time you ask.** A tenant who has already published
one must not be told to publish a different one.

left_at.description:
Set when they left. **The record stays** — they are on last year's
payroll and whatever they approved.

reports_to.description: Who they report to. Absent for the root.

secret.description: The same secret, for typing in when a camera will not co-operate.

uri.description: Render as a QR code. Every authenticator app reads this.

closed.description: `spent`, `expired`, `revoked`, or absent while it is live.

deferred.description: What was deferred when it was granted.

outstanding.description: **What is still owed to the customer.**

annual_days.description:
Days of paid annual leave this year. **21, or 30 after five years'
service** — and the step can land mid-year, in which case this is the
two rates over the days each applied to.

annual_left.description:
What is left. **May be negative**, which is a real state — somebody who
took three weeks in January and left in March has overdrawn, and a
clamp to zero would hide the money the business is owed back.

annual_taken.description: Annual days already taken in the window, from `hr`.

days_in_window.description:
Days of the window they were employed for. Fewer than 365 for a joiner
or a leaver, and the entitlement is pro-rated by it.

served_days.description:
How long they had served when the window opened, in days. Returned so
the figure above can be checked.

position.description:
Where it landed in the log. A client that wants to read its own write
back passes this as `?consistent_after=`.

erased.description: Rows removed, current and superseded together.

deliveries.description:
How many times they have sent it. More than one means their retries are
not being acknowledged, or they simply retry regardless.

event_id.description: **The provider's own id.** What makes a retry a retry.

days_left.description:
**Negative once it has gone.** A screen that showed "0 days left" for
both tomorrow and last March is the screen somebody stops reading.

FieldSet.description: Every field a business has added.

fields.description: **The order is yours**, and it is the order a form shows them in.

FieldView.description: One field a business has added to its customers.

key.description: The stable machine name. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores.

max.description: **Characters**, on a `text` field. Ignored on every other kind.

options.description: What may be chosen, on a `choice` field.

required.description:
Whether a customer is expected to have one. **Reported, not enforced** —
see `Fields::missing_from`.

checksum.description: SHA-256, hex. Checked on every download.

engine.description:
Which engine holds it. **Not a URL** — fetch it from
`/v1/files/{id}/content`.

owner_kind.description:
What it is attached to — `invoice`, `bill`, `reservation`, `customer`,
`employee`, `entry` or `tenant`.

removed_at.description: Set when it was taken off. The record stays either way.

period.description: The period, as it identifies itself: `SAR.2026-01-01.2026-04-01`.

reference.description: ZATCA's acknowledgement, once clearance exists to produce one.

skipped.description:
Already there, and left exactly as they were. Not a failure — fitting
out twice is meant to be harmless.

FreeView.description: How much of one service is free over a span.

free.description:
How many more bookings fit across the **whole** span.

Zero means full. It is what was free a moment ago, not a reservation —
the answer that counts is the one taking the booking computes under
locks, and a form that treats this as a promise will occasionally show a
slot that has just gone.

signed_xml.description:
**The document as submitted**: those bytes plus the signature, the QR
and the `cac:Signature` that points at it.

stamped_xml.description:
**The document ZATCA stamped, base64** — the one a buyer must be given.
Cleared standard invoices only.

xml.description: The canonical UBL that was hashed, and what the signature covers.

advance_for.description:
**What a deposit was taken for**, when it does not. Exactly one of the
two is present, and a settled deposit has both — its own prepayment
invoice, and the booking it secures.

failed_why.description: In the gateway's words, when it refused.

fee.description:
What the gateway kept. Absent until it says, which for most providers is
not until the payout.

invoice.description: The invoice, when it collects against one.

pay_at.description:
**Where the customer goes to pay**, while there is somewhere: the
checkout the worker opened at a provider that hosts one, or the 3-D
Secure page a saved-card charge raised. `null` until the gateway has
said, and for a charge that needs nobody.

source.description:
Themselves, or somebody beneath them. **The first question anybody asks
of an inherited permission is where it came from.**

Imported.description:
What an import did.

**Partial failure is the outcome and not an exception.** A thousand-row file
with three bad rows imports 997 and returns the three; refusing the file
means a person fixing a spreadsheet by bisection.

imported.description:
Rows that went in, including ones that were already there — a re-upload
of a corrected file is meant to be safe, so a row that was imported last
time counts as imported this time.

rejected.description: Rows that did not, with the row number and the reason.

currency.description: The currency every account is opened in.

accept_path.description:
Where the token goes, so a client does not have to build the URL itself
and get it subtly wrong.

On the **apex**, not the tenant's subdomain: the recipient may have no
account anywhere yet.

token.description:
**Shown once.** Pass it on however you already talk to this person.
Nothing stores it, so a lost link is re-issued rather than recovered.

tax_breakdown.description: One row per rate, which is what a Saudi tax invoice has to print.

cancelled_on.description:
Set once a credit note has cancelled it. A cancelled invoice owes
nothing, and `outstanding` says so too.

id.description: The key the client sent when issuing, and what addresses this invoice.

number.description: The statutory number. Sequential, gapless, and what the document prints.

payment_count.description:
How many payments have been recorded. The payments themselves are on
`GET /v1/sales/invoices/{invoice}`.

Not `payments`: the detail view flattens this one and adds the list, and
two shapes under one name on the same resource is a client generator's
worst afternoon.

Issued.description: A statutory document that now exists.

id.description: The key you sent, which is what addresses this document from here on.

number.description:
The statutory number, allocated here from the tenant's gapless series.
What goes on the printed document.

On a repeated request this is the number the document already has, not a
new one — the series does not move for a retry.

position.description:
Where it landed in the log. A client that wants to read its own write
back passes this as `?consistent_after=`.

secret.description: **Shown once.** There is no way to read it again, by design.

expires_at.description: Set by a rotation on the key being replaced. This is the overlap window.

last_used_at.description:
Best effort, so it can be a little behind. Enough to answer "is anything
still using this" before somebody revokes it.

public_key.description: **Safe anywhere.** It identifies an integration and proves nothing.

rotated_from.description: The key this one replaced, when it came from a rotation.

taken.description:
Days taken per kind over the window. **What a balance is drawn down
by** — how much somebody is *entitled* to is statute, and belongs to the
country module.

amount.description:
The most one invoice, credit note or refund may come to. More than
nothing. A document in another currency is refused as well, because it
cannot be compared with this.

basis.description: `before_vat` or `after_vat`: which of a document's totals is compared.

LimitsView.description:
The rules, in order. **The first that matches decides**, so an exception
goes above the refusal it is an exception to.

rules.name: A bookkeeper posts under ten thousand

rules.description:
Each is `{ name, when, then }`. `then` is `refuse`, or `allow` — which
only ever restores what the role already permits. `when` asks about
`amount` (money), `branch` (a branch id), `capability` (`read`,
`post_entries`, `manage_accounts`) or `role` (`owner`, `accountant`,
`clerk`, `viewer`), and combines with `all`, `any`, `not` and `always`.
An amount in another currency than the one compared against has no
answer, and no answer refuses: a `refuse` rule in `SAR` refuses an entry
in `USD` it would otherwise judge, and an `allow` in `USD` excepts
nothing in `SAR`. A tenant that posts in two currencies puts an `allow`
per currency above the refusal.

LineAllowance.description: Something taken off a line, and why.

amount.description: What comes off, in minor units and positive. `2500` is 25.00 SAR.

reason.description: A customer reads this, so it is text and not a code.

LineCharge.description:
What to charge for a line, before the tenant's price bands.

**The rate is yours; the band is the tenant's.** Which hours cost more is
configuration, resolved when the booking is written and frozen onto it, so
a client cannot decide its own peak rate.

currency.description: ISO 4217. Every amount on the booking must be in it.

quantity.description: How many. Four covers, twelve places, three nights.

rate.description: The list rate for one of these, in minor units.

vat_rate.description:
Basis points — 1500 is 15%. The rate that applied when it was issued, not
today's.

ListRate.description: A published price on the wire.

code.description: The tenant's own batch code, on a lot-tracked product.

expires_on.description:
Absent on a batch with no shelf life. Those go out after every dated
lot, oldest first.

name.description:
The product's name, as declared. `null` only when the read model holds
no declaration for it: the lot is still listed.

serials.description: The units still on this lot, on a serial-tracked product.

value.description: What the remainder is carried at.

customer.description: The `crm` record this invoice's buyer turned out to be.

module_roles.description: Where the tenant said something different. Usually empty.

role.description:
What they are here, and in any module not listed below.

One of `owner`, `accountant`, `clerk`, `viewer`.

MessageArg.description:
A value interpolated into a message.

Typed rather than pre-formatted strings, because formatting is
locale-dependent: a count selects a plural form, a date renders differently
under a Hijri calendar, and money carries a currency whose symbol placement
varies. Handing the renderer a `String` throws away everything it needs.

oneOf.description:
Latin-script text — an identifier, a slug, a code. Bidi-isolated when
rendered into an RTL locale.

value.description:
Latin-script text — an identifier, a slug, a code. Bidi-isolated when
rendered into an RTL locale.

oneOf.description: A plain number, not a count. Does not select a plural form.

value.description: A plain number, not a count. Does not select a plural form.

oneOf.description: A quantity. Selects the plural form of the template.

value.description: A quantity. Selects the plural form of the template.

deprecated.description:
Set when the module is no longer offered, and says why. A tenant that has
it keeps it; nobody new can turn it on.

requires.description:
What this module needs underneath it, all of it. A client building a
picker needs this to grey out the impossible combinations rather than
let someone discover them.

requires_any.description: What this module needs **at least one** of. Empty for most.

stage.description:
`reserved`, `confirmed`, `arrived`, `in_service`, `completed`,
`cancelled` or `no_show`. Moving to the stage it is already in is a
no-op.

why.description: Why. Kept and shown, and it is what a cancellation reason goes in.

expected.description:
What the books said was there — on the lot, or on the shelf for a count
of the shelf. Set on a count, and frozen as it was found.

kind.description:
`received` (bought in, or put back by a credit note), `consumed` (sold
on a document), `written_off` or `counted`.

lot.description:
Which lot this came off, or went back onto. **Absent only where no lot
was involved** — units a plain product's sale took that no lot could
cover (R1), the part of a return or a count of the shelf that settles
that debt, and the one row a count of the shelf leaves when it moved
nothing.

quantity.description:
Signed: what this movement did to what is on hand. The movements sum to
the quantity above, lot by lot.

reference.description: The request or document this movement was for.

uses.description:
Every `{{ binding }}` this template uses, in the order it uses them.
Answered so a caller editing one does not have to parse the bodies.

code.description: The account code, as the tenant numbers their chart.

currency.description:
ISO 4217. An account holds one currency, and postings in another are
refused.

kind.description:
`asset`, `liability`, `equity`, `revenue` or `expense`. Decides which
side of the account a positive balance sits on.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. `SA` for a Saudi buyer.

billed_on.description: The tax point, from their document. Not when you typed it in.

reference.description:
**The supplier's own invoice number.** What a reclaim is evidenced by.
Recording the same one twice for the same supplier is refused: it would
be a duplicate claim.

account.description:
The expense or asset account this lands in. One bill routinely covers
several. **Ignored when `product` names a stocked product** — that line
lands in the goods-received-not-invoiced account the delivery credited.

product.description:
**The stocked product this line bought**, if it bought one.

Leave it off for anything that is not stock, which is most lines. With
it, the line posts against the delivery rather than to `account`: the
receipt already debited inventory and credited
`2010 Goods received, not invoiced`, and this is the invoice clearing
it. It works in either order — a bill that arrives before its delivery
leaves `2010` a debit, which is *invoiced, not yet received* — and
nothing about a supplier invoice is blocked by a delivery that has not
turned up. A product nobody declared is refused.

tax.description:
**The tax the supplier charged, in minor units.** Not computed here: a
reclaim is evidenced by their document, so the figure in the books has to
be the figure on it. Must be zero on anything not standard-rated.

vat.description: `standard`, `zero` or `exempt`, as the supplier treated it.

vat_rate.description:
The rate they charged, in basis points. 1500 is 15%.

Recorded rather than resolved. If it disagrees with today's statutory
rate that is a thing worth being able to see, not a thing to correct
silently.

account.description: The cash or bank account it left.

reference.description:
Your own reference — a transfer number, a cheque. Recording the same one
twice against the same bill is a no-op.

branch.description:
Which branch it is at. Omit it in a single-branch business.

**Set once**: a chair that physically moves is a new resource, because
changing this would re-attribute every booking it ever held to a place
it was not at.

capacity.description:
How many can be held at once. One stylist, six covers at a table, eight
rooms of a type, five hundred places in a museum slot.

employee.description:
Which member of staff this is, when the business keeps staff records.

**Set once**, for the same reason `branch` is: a chair booked as "Sara"
is not the same resource once it is "Noura".

Optional, and a diary works without it. What naming somebody buys is
that assigning them is refused once a work document has lapsed — an
expired iqama means a person who may not legally be rostered.

id.description: Your key for this resource. Declaring the same one twice is a no-op.

kind.description: `person`, `place` or `thing`. Display only — no rule branches on it.

oneOf.description:
**The published price, before tax.** What the public site shows and
what a public booking is priced at — a stranger cannot send a price —
and so what a deposit is a fraction of. Absent for a business that
bills elsewhere.

mechanic.description:
`points`, `stamps` or `visits`. It decides what produces the count and
nothing after that — the accounting is the same for all three.

branch.description:
Where it applies. Absent is company-wide, which is not the same as some
particular branch.

propagates.description:
Whether it travels up the reporting line. Defaults to yes, which is the
rule; a claim on the segregation-of-duties list never travels whatever
is sent.

NewComponent.description: One part of what somebody is paid, or has taken off.

what.description: The business's own word for it: `بدل سكن`, `Transport`, `Advance`.

declared.description: What was actually counted in the drawer.

NewCreditLine.description: One line of a credit note: which invoice line, and how much of it.

against.description:
**Which line of the invoice this credits**, counting from zero.

The description and the tax treatment come from it. That is the point:
a credit note can only describe something the invoice charged for, and
is credited at the rate that invoice carried — one issued at 5% is
credited at 5% for ever.

amount.description:
Excluding tax, and positive — stated the way the invoice stated it
rather than as a negative. May be less than the line: part of a line
can come back.

quantity.description:
**How many units came back onto the shelf**, when the invoice line sold
stock. Optional, and never worked out from `amount`: a partial credit is
as often a price adjustment as a returned carton, and the two are
different statements. Leave it out and nothing goes back on the shelf.

serials.description:
**Which units came back**, on a line that sold serial-tracked stock:
one name per unit, as many as `quantity`. Each must be one this invoice
line sold and that has not come back already. Leave it out and the
units come back by quantity, which for named units only the whole line
can.

id.description:
**Your own key for this cancellation, not the credit note's number.**
Sending the same one twice is a no-op; a different one against an invoice
that is already credited is refused.

The credit note's number is allocated here, from its own gapless series —
ZATCA numbers credit notes separately from the invoices they credit.

on.description:
When the credit is treated as happening. Usually today, not the date of
the invoice.

oneOf.description:
Where they are, as they are today. Snapshotted onto the invoice, so a
customer moving does not rewrite what was already issued.

ZATCA wants street, city and country on a standard invoice; without them
it accepts the document and warns, which is a warning that becomes a
finding at an inspection.

id.description:
The `crm` customer this is for. Optional, and checked when it is given:
an id naming no record, or an archived one, refuses the invoice.

The fields below are still yours and are still what gets printed. The
reference is for grouping; the copy is what the document says.

vat_number.description:
The buyer's VAT registration number, printed on the invoice.

**Giving one makes this a standard invoice**, which ZATCA clears before
the buyer may be given it. Leaving it out makes it a simplified one,
reported within twenty-four hours.

kind.description: `person` or `company`. Only a company may carry a VAT number.

registered_on.description: When they became a customer. Defaults to now.

minutes.description:
Minutes worked. **Zero is an absence somebody recorded deliberately**,
which is a different fact from a day with no record at all.

NewDeposit.description:
A deposit: what it secures, what it comes to before tax, and who it is
billed to.

**The net is sent, not the gross alone.** A deposit is a fraction of
something already priced, and the price had a net; working the net back out
of a total does not always land, so it travels with the deposit instead. The
`amount` charged must equal this plus the tax on it, and settling refuses if
it does not.

against.description: What it secures — a booking. Opaque to this module.

buyer_name.description: The buyer, as the prepayment invoice will print them.

buyer_vat_number.description: Giving one makes it a standard invoice rather than a simplified one.

net.description: **Before tax**, in minor units. The prepayment invoice is raised for it.

recipient.description: Whoever the device belongs to, in whatever id space the caller uses.

amount.description:
Minor units, **positive**: what comes off. A negative one is a charge,
which this system does not issue.

reason.description: Why, printed on the invoice — ZATCA shows it to the customer.

vat.description:
Which treatment it comes off: `standard`, `zero` or `exempt`.

**A discount reduces the tax only on what carried any.** Discounting the
standard-rated part of a mixed invoice is a different number from
discounting the exempt part, so the invoice has to say which.

expires_on.description:
**The last day it is valid**, inclusive — a document that says it expires
on the 30th is valid on the 30th, which is what it means and what the
person holding it will argue.

A date and not a timestamp: an iqama expires on a day in Riyadh, not at
an hour in UTC.

number.description: Its number, as printed on it.

domain.description: The registrable domain, with no scheme and no port.

employees.description:
Who is in the run.

**The caller says, and that is deliberate.** Enumerating employees means
reading `hr`'s read model, and a payroll run is money leaving the
business — it must not be computed from a table that may be a second
behind. List staff from `GET /v1/hr/employees` and send the ones to pay.

performed.description:
What each of them performed in the period, net.

From `GET /v1/booking/reservations` — or, once it exists as a route,
whatever reports completed priced work per person. Omit it for a
business that pays no commission, which is most of them.

**The amount is not yours to send.** What fraction of this somebody
earns is the rate on their salary, read from their own record, so a
caller can be wrong about the *basis* and never about the *commission*.

period.description:
`YYYY-MM`. The entry posts on the **last day of it**, not the day the
run was approved: a February run approved in March belongs in February.

count.description:
How many counts. Omit it for points, which are computed from the
scheme's rate at this card's rank; send it for stamps and visits, which
count their own.

from.description: The sale it came from. Opaque, and not checked.

reference.description: Your key for this movement. Sending it twice is a no-op.

spend.description:
**What was spent, excluding tax.** Part of it is deferred to the counts
this awards, which is IFRS 15's separate performance obligation.

branch.description:
**Where they work**, which is not the `X-Branch` on this request. That
one says where the request happened; this says where the person is.

reports_to.description:
Who they report to. Absent makes them the root, of which a business has
one — whoever nobody reports to.

against.description: The thing it is held against — the booking a deposit secures. Opaque.

reason.description:
`bought`, `gifted_by_customer`, `granted_by_business` or
`free_from_coupon`. The last two carry no value: nobody paid, so there
is nothing to defer.

uses.description: Uses granted. Absent for a deposit, which is an amount and not a count.

value.description: **What is deferred, excluding tax.** Zero when nobody paid.

what.description: What it is for, in your own words.

lines.description:
Must sum to zero, in one currency. An unbalanced set is a 400 carrying
the difference.

occurred_on.description: The date the business treats this as happening — not a clock reading.

filed_on.description:
The date the business treats the filing as made. Not a clock reading, for
the same reason a tax point is not one.

from.description: The first day of the period, on the tenant's calendar.

until.description:
**Exclusive.**
The first day **after** the period: consecutive returns neither
overlap nor leave a day out.

NewGateway.description:
What a tenant hands over so this system can talk to their gateway.

Shaped per provider, because the three need different things: Moyasar a
secret key, Tabby a key **and** the merchant code its integration manager
issued, Tamara a token and which host it belongs to.

sandbox.description:
Tamara only. Their sandbox is a different host rather than a different
token.

secret.description:
The secret key, or Tamara's API token. **Stored sealed and never
readable again.**

NewGatewayPayment.description:
**Not `sales`' `NewPayment`.** That one is a customer handing over money;
this is a charge created at a gateway, which may never become one. The
`OpenAPI` document keeps one schema per name, so the two have to be told
apart — see `no_two_modules_claim_the_same_schema_name`.

amount.description: Minor units — halalas for SAR. Never a decimal.

oneOf.description:
**A deposit**, when nothing has been billed yet. Settling it raises a
prepayment invoice, because receiving the money is itself a tax point.

gateway_id.description:
**The gateway's own id**, from the charge you created against it. Every
callback names this and nothing else, so a payment recorded without one
can never be settled.

invoice.description:
The invoice this is collecting against. **Exactly one of this and
`advance_for`.**

started_at.description: When the charge was created. Defaults to now.

amount.description: Minor units. Omit to give back everything that is left.

reason.description:
Why, in the customer's language. **It is printed on the credit note**
and reaches ZATCA as the document's note, so "damaged in transit" is
worth more than the default.

reference.description:
Your own reference for this refund. Sending it again is a retry, not a
second refund — **and it is the credit note's key too**, so a retry does
not issue a second document either.

handle.description: The address to invite. Also the login handle they will end up with.

currency.description: ISO 4217. Every line is in this currency.

customer.description:
Copied onto the invoice as values, never as a reference. A tax invoice
is a legal document; last year's copy must not change when a customer
record does.

discounts.description:
What comes off the whole invoice, printed as its own figure rather than
folded into a smaller total.

**The tax comes off with it.** A 15 discount on a standard-rated invoice
reduces the taxable amount by 15 and the tax by 2.25 — which is why a
discount is not a negative line, and why it has to say which treatment
it comes off.

issued_on.description: The tax point. A date the business chose, not a clock reading.

lines.description: At least one line that comes to something.

allowances.description:
What comes off **this line**, each printed as its own figure.

No treatment on them: the line already says how it is taxed, so an
allowance on it reduces the taxable amount at that line's rate. A
discount on the whole *document* is the other field, and that one has to
name which treatment it comes off.

lot.description:
**Which lot** to take the units from, overriding the picking rule — a
scanned batch, or stock promised to this customer. The lot's `id` as
`GET /v1/inventory/lots` lists it, not its batch code. A line that names
one must also name the `product`; a lot that is not open at this branch,
or that holds fewer than the line takes, is refused. Leave it out and
the earliest expiry goes first.

net.description:
Minor units, in the invoice's currency. Excluding tax, and **before this
line's own allowances** — what is charged is this less them.

**Per unit when `quantity` is given**, and the whole line otherwise. The
line comes to `net × quantity`, worked out here and never divided back
out: going backwards from a total is a division that does not always
land on a whole halala, and the tax document has to balance.

product.description:
**What this line sells off a shelf**, when it sells one: the product's
id, as `/v1/inventory/products` declared it.

Optional. A line with one depletes that product's stock at this branch
in the same transaction as the invoice, and books what it cost; a line
without one behaves exactly as before. A product nobody declared is
refused rather than ignored.

quantity.description:
**How many units.** Optional: leave it out and the line is a single
amount charged once, which is what every invoice issued before this
field existed is.

serials.description:
**Which units**, on a serial-tracked product — one name per unit, as
they were received. A line that names any must also name the `product`
and charge for exactly that many. A name that is not on the shelf —
unknown, already sold, written off — is refused.

vat.description:
`standard`, `zero` or `exempt`. The *rate* is not a client's to choose —
it is statutory, and resolved here. Zero-rated and exempt are both 0%
and mean different things on a return, so both are kept.

name.description: What a person calls it, so revoking the right one does not need a guess.

role.description:
The role its machine identity holds — `owner`, `accountant`, `clerk` or
`viewer`.

**The scopes can only narrow this.** A key given a viewer's role and a
scope that permits posting still cannot post, because the role is
checked as well.

One of `owner`, `accountant`, `clerk`, `viewer`.

until.description: **Inclusive**: the 3rd to the 5th is three days.

lot.description:
Which lot the units come off, when the till overrides the picking rule
— a scanned batch. The lot's `id`; a line that names one must also name
the `product`, and a lot that is not open here or is short is refused.

net.description:
Before tax, in the sale's currency. **The rate is not yours to send**:
it is the tenant's configured one, resolved inside the write, so an
invoice cannot be stamped with a rate that was never current.

**Per unit when `quantity` is given**, and the whole line otherwise —
the till rings a price and says how many.

product.description:
The product this rings off the shelf, when the till sells stock.
Optional: the shelf comes down and the cost is booked in the same write
as the sale, and a line without one behaves exactly as before.

quantity.description: How many. Optional; one when it is left out.

serials.description:
Which units, on a serial-tracked product — one name per unit. A line
that names any must also name the `product` and ring exactly that many.

amount.description: Minor units, **positive**: what comes off this line.

reason.description: Why, printed on the invoice — ZATCA shows it to the customer.

rate_bp.description:
The base earning rate, in counts per major unit spent, in basis points.
`10_000` is one point per riyal. Ignored for stamps and visits.

tiers.description:
Ranks, in any order. The highest `from` at or below a card's lifetime
count wins; below all of them the base rate applies.

worth.description:
**What one count is worth when it is redeemed**, and the currency every
card under this scheme is held in. It is the standalone selling price
the IFRS 15 allocation is computed from, so it decides how much of each
sale is deferred.

email.description:
Their login. If it already belongs to someone, that account gains access
rather than a second one being created for the same person.

password.description:
Chosen by the owner and handed over. An invitation flow would leave this
to the recipient — see `erp-control/src/members.rs`.

extra.description: Anything the caller resolved itself. `link` is the usual one.

key.description:
**The caller's key**, and what makes a retry one message rather than
two.

language.description: `english` or `arabic`. Omitted takes the tenant's own.

operator.description: Which identity, when the template is addressed to an operator.

topic.description:
What it is about, and which one. The **only** thing a caller supplies
about content.

origin.description:
Exactly what a browser sends in `Origin`: scheme, host, and a port only
when it is not the scheme's default. It is echoed back verbatim, so a
trailing slash or a path makes it a different string and it will not
match.

NewPartialCreditNote.description: A credit note against part of an invoice.

on.description:
The credit note's **own** tax point — the period it falls in. Usually
today, and not the invoice's date.

reference.description:
**Your own key for this credit note, not its number.** Sending the same
one twice is a no-op. The number is allocated here, from the same
gapless series a cancellation draws on.
Your key. Sending it twice is a no-op.

to.description: The account code the money went to.

account.description: The cash or bank account it landed in.

reference.description:
The payer's or the bank's reference. Recording the same one twice against
the same invoice is a no-op.

amount.description: **What arrived.** Minor units — the number on the bank statement.

covers.description:
The gateway payment ids it covers.

**Empty is allowed and reconciles nothing** — right for somebody typing
from a bank statement, who has an amount and no transaction list. The
answer says `covered: 0` rather than pretending it agreed.

into.description: The bank account it landed in.

reference.description: The gateway's own id for the transfer.
Your key for this redemption. Sending it twice is a no-op.

toward.description: What they were spent on. Opaque, and not checked.

tracking.description:
**Frozen.** `none`, `lot` or `serial`; `none` when absent. A lot-tracked
delivery names its batch and may name an expiry; a serial-tracked one
names every unit.

unit.description:
**Frozen.** What one of these is — `gram`, `piece`, `bottle`. Every
quantity ever recorded against this product is a number in it, and there
is no route that changes it.

code.description:
The batch this came in, in the tenant's own words. Required on a
lot-tracked product and refused on any other. It may repeat: the lot's
own id keeps two deliveries of one code apart.

expires_on.description:
When this batch goes off. Only on a lot-tracked product, and only when
the batch has a shelf life — an undated lot goes out after every dated
one, oldest first.

quantity.description: A whole number of the product's own unit.

serials.description:
One per unit, on a serial-tracked product. **Yours, not ours**: a serial
is an identity and this system does not invent identities.

value.description: What the **whole** delivery cost, not what one unit did.

reference.description: Your key for this redemption. Sending it twice is a no-op.

uses.description: How many uses. Defaults to one, and is ignored on a deposit.

account.description: The cash or bank account it went out of.

reason.description:
Why, in the customer's language. **Printed on the credit note** and sent
to ZATCA as the document's note, so a real sentence is worth more than
the default.

reference.description:
Your reference for handing the money back. Sending the same one twice
against the same invoice is a no-op — **and it keys the credit note
too**, so a retry does not issue a second document.

at.description: When the booking was taken. Defaults to now.

customer.description: The `crm` record, when there is one. A walk-in has none.

customer_name.description:
What the diary prints. Frozen, so a customer changing their name next
year does not rewrite last year's calendar.

oneOf.description: What to charge. Absent for a business that bills elsewhere.

takes.description: Everything this line takes at once — the stylist *and* the chair.

until.description:
Exclusive, so a line ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 are
back to back and do not clash.

what.description: What the business calls it. Never looked at by any rule here.

lines.description:
Which lines are coming back. **Empty is the whole sale.** With lines,
the tenders must come to exactly what those lines credit, tax included.

reference.description: Your key. Sending it twice is a no-op.

tenders.description:
What the customer is handed back, and how. Must come to what is being
credited: the whole sale without `lines`, those lines with.

occurred_on.description:
When the correction is treated as happening. Usually today, not the date
of the mistake — reversing into a closed period is how a filed return
stops matching the books.

allowances.description:
Added: housing, transport, a phone.

**Amounts, not percentages.** A housing allowance quoted as 25% of basic
is sent as the riyals it comes to, because a rate stored here would be
recomputed on every run and a basic-pay rise would silently restate last
month's payslip.

basic.description: Basic pay for a full month.

commission_bp.description:
What fraction of the work they perform they earn, in basis points.
`500` is five per cent. Absent or zero is a business that pays none.

**A rate and not an amount**, unlike the allowances above: a commission
is a share of a number that changes every month, and storing the amount
would mean restating it each period.

deductions.description:
Taken off: an advance being repaid, a loan.

**Not tax and not GOSI.** Those are statutory and computed from the
gross by the country module; a business that could type them in here
would be able to get them wrong.

customer.description:
Who it is for. A walk-in is a name and nothing else; **a VAT number makes
this a standard invoice**, which ZATCA clears before the customer may be
given it.

tenders.description:
How it was paid. Must come to **exactly** the sale: less would leave a
balance owing, which is an invoice on credit and not a till sale, and
change handed back is a counter concern rather than a record.

NewSavedCard.description:
A card a customer has agreed to leave on file.

**The token is minted in the customer's browser**, against the publishable
key, and it is the only part of a card this system ever holds. There is no
field here for a card number and there will not be one — sending one to a
merchant backend is grounds for Moyasar terminating the agreement.

last4.description: The last four digits, and only those.

provider.description: `moyasar`. Buy-now-pay-later providers have no card to keep.

token.description:
**The gateway's token**, from tokenizing the card in the browser. Stored
sealed and never returned by any route.

NewSavedCardCharge.description: What somebody wants taken off a card that is already on file.

amount.description: Minor units — halalas for SAR. Never a decimal.

callback_url.description:
**Where the customer lands if the gateway decides it needs them.** A
saved-card charge usually completes with nobody watching; one that
raises a 3-D Secure challenge does not, and a charge with nowhere to
send them is one that can never finish.

oneOf.description:
A deposit, when there is no invoice. A saved card is exactly how a
returning customer's deposit gets charged.

invoice.description:
The invoice this is collecting against. **Exactly one of this and
`advance_for`.**

NewSchedule.description:
What to set the schedule to.

**Its own type, without `configured`.** The answer says whether anybody has
confirmed the numbers; the request cannot, because sending it *is* the
confirmation. One type for both would accept a field it ignored, which is a
caller believing they said something.

secret.description:
The shared secret, as the provider shows it. Stored sealed, and never
readable again.

float.description: What is in the drawer before anything is sold.

till.description: Your own name for this counter.

shifts.description:
**The whole pattern**, replacing what was there.

One at a time is not offered, for the reason skills are not: an empty
list means *no pattern recorded*, so adding one window would restrict
somebody a caller was only trying to note a Saturday for.

skills.description:
**The whole set**, replacing what was there.

One at a time is deliberately not offered: an empty list means *no
restriction*, so recording the first skill starts restricting — and a
caller adding one would eventually give somebody a single skill they
were only trying to note and take everything else away.

Each is the id of the bookable resource that service is.

email.description: The login of an account that already exists, and has a second factor.

declared.description:
What was actually there. On a serial-tracked product, how many units
`serials` names.

lot.description:
**Which lot was counted**, for someone counting batches. Leave it out to
count the shelf — see the `count` operation's description.

serials.description:
The units found, by name, on a serial-tracked product. What was on hand
and is not named here leaves as missing.

price.description: **What is deferred, excluding tax**, for this term.

vat_number.description:
Their VAT registration number. **Required if any line carries tax** —
input VAT is reclaimed against a registered supplier's tax invoice, and a
bill without one is not evidence of a reclaim.

method.description:
`cash`, `card` or `transfer`. **Only cash is in the drawer**, so only
cash changes what the count should come to.

NewVerification.description: A number to send a code to.

phone.description:
E.164, or something a person would write that reads as one — spaces,
dashes and a leading `00` are all fine. A national number is refused
rather than repaired: `0500000000` is a Saudi number to a Saudi reader
and nothing at all to a message gateway.

lot.description:
Which lot to take it from, overriding earliest-expiry-first. A lot that
cannot cover it is refused rather than topped up from the next.

quantity.description:
How many. On a product tracked by quantity, and refused on a
serial-tracked one.

serials.description: Which units. On a serial-tracked product, and refused on any other.

branch.description:
Only when this business wants its invoices distinct per branch: the
branch this unit belongs to (for a VAT group member, their own
10-digit TIN). Absent, the unit is the whole business and carries its
registered name.

environment.description:
`sandbox`, `simulation` or `production`. **Not a default** — the only
visible difference is a string in the request, and a mistake onboards
into the wrong authority rather than failing.

oneOf.description: The samples, once they all passed for the current certificate.

live.description: Whether it can clear and report real invoices.

reached.description: Which stages this tenant has credentials for: `compliance`, `production`.

oneOf.description: What ZATCA refused about the current certificate, if anything.

state.description:
`none`, `checking` (the worker is submitting samples or asking for the
production certificate), `refused` (ZATCA said no — see `refusal`), or
`live`.

closes_at.description:
Minutes past local midnight, exclusive. `1020` is 17:00, and a booking
may run right up to it.

days.description: 1 to 31. Empty means every day of the month.

from.description: The first day these hours apply. Absent means they always have.

Paged_AgedCustomerView.description:
One page of a list, and where the next one starts.

# Why every list is shaped like this

Because the alternative was a bare array that stopped at 200 and said
nothing. A tenant with 201 invoices saw 200 and had no way to tell — the
response looked exactly like a complete one, which is the worst shape a bug
can have.

`next` absent means **the list ended**. Present means pass it back as
`?after=` to continue.

items.description: One customer's debt, split by how late it is.

customer.description: A name to show: the one the most recent invoice in this group froze.

identified.description:
Whether `key` is a customer id.

`false` means these invoices were grouped by the name they froze, so two
spellings of one buyer are two rows. Record them in `crm` and reference
them to merge.

key.description:
What this row is grouped under: a customer id, or the frozen name when
the invoices named no record.

oldest_due.description:
The due date of the oldest unpaid invoice. What a collections call opens
with.

total.description: Every bucket together, in this currency.

next.description:
Pass back as `?after=` for the next page. Absent when there are no more.

Opaque: what is in it is the query's business, and a client that parsed
one would break the day a list is ordered differently.

PaymentRecorded.description:
Something recorded against a document, which is not a document itself.

A payment carries no statutory number: the invoice it settles is the numbered
thing, and a receipt references that.

id.description: The invoice it was recorded against.

difference.description:
What arrived less what the covered payments said should have.
**Negative is short.**

covered.description: Zero reconciles nothing, which is not the same as agreeing.

commission.description:
Earned on work performed, at the rate on their salary. **Part of
`gross`**, because statutory contributions are computed from what
somebody earned rather than from the predictable part of it.

name.description:
**As it was when the run was made.** A payslip says who it was for, and
somebody who marries next month does not get a new copy of last month's.

performed.description: What the commission was earned on, so the number can be checked.

company.description:
What you are being invited to, and as what. A link that does not say is
a link people accept without reading.

has_account.description:
`true` when that address already has an account here — so the form asks
for the existing password rather than offering to choose a new one.

commission.description: Part of `gross`, not on top of it.

net.description: Net of what they completed, in minor units.

channels.description: Where this person wants to hear about it. `in_system` is the bell.

position.description:
The log position this landed at. Pass it to a read as
`?consistent_after=`.

example.detail: Those login details are not right. Please try again.
example.title: Unauthorized

args.description:
The values the message names, typed — which account, which module, how
much was outstanding. A client that renders its own sentence reads these
instead of parsing `detail`. Absent when the message takes none.

code.description: The stable identifier. Branch on this, never on `detail`.

detail.description: The message in the caller's language, chosen by `Accept-Language`.

type.description:
`https://errors.erp.example/` followed by the code. Stable, and a place
to look it up — see `docs/ERRORS.md` for every code this API can answer
with.

PublicBookingView.description: What a stranger may do on this tenant's public booking site.

deposit_bp.description:
The deposit, as a fraction of the booking's net in basis points. `0` is
no deposit; `10000` is the whole price.

hold_minutes.description:
How long an unpaid slot is held before it lapses. `0` is indefinitely,
which is right only when no deposit is asked for.

open.description:
Whether the public site takes bookings at all. Off until somebody turns
it on: the absence of a setting is a no.

verify_phone.description: Whether a public booker must prove their phone number first.

PublicLine.description: One slot a customer is asking for.

until.description:
Exclusive, so a line ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 are back
to back and do not clash.

what.description: What the customer calls it, for the diary. Never read by any rule.

PublicReservation.description: A booking a customer makes for themselves.

code.description:
**The code sent to `customer_phone`**, when the business asks for one.

Required only if this business has turned phone verification on. Ignored
when they have not, so a site that never asks for a code keeps working.

customer_name.description:
What the diary prints. **No `customer` id**, unlike the counter's
version: a stranger does not get to say which of a business's customer
records they are, and accepting one would let anybody attach a booking
to somebody else's file.

PublicReservationTaken.description: What a customer is told after booking.

deposit_bp.description:
What the business asks for to hold it, in basis points of the booking's
net. **Zero unless configured** (`PUT /v1/booking/public-settings`).
When it is not zero the slot is held unpaid for the configured
`hold_minutes` and lapses unless the deposit is paid through
`POST /v1/booking/public/reservations/{reservation}/deposit`; it is
secured when the money settles. Here so a site can say what will be
asked, not so it can claim it was taken.

stage.description:
Always `reserved`. **A public booking is never confirmed by the act of
making it** — the business confirms, which is the whole difference
between a request and a promise.

resource.description: The stylist, room or table. It has to be declared.

why.description: Why, for whoever has to refuse the booking. Required.

exempt_reason.description:
**Why your exempt supplies carry no tax.** In Saudi Arabia a landlord
letting residential property is `VATEX-SA-30` (real estate
transactions); a financial services business is `VATEX-SA-29`.

Required before an exempt invoice can be issued. See
[`Self::zero_reason`].

standard.description:
The standard rate in **basis points**. 1500 is 15% (Saudi Arabia), 500
is 5% (the UAE).

Zero-rated and exempt are 0% by definition and not configurable — a
jurisdiction that taxed an exempt supply would not call it exempt.

Applies to invoices issued **from now on**. Every document already issued
carries the rate it was issued under, so changing this cannot restate a
filed return.

zero_reason.description:
**Why your zero-rated supplies carry no tax**, as the tax authority's
own code. In Saudi Arabia one of ZATCA's `VATEX-SA-*` codes — an
exporter of goods is `VATEX-SA-32`, a private school teaching citizens
is `VATEX-SA-EDU`.

Required before a zero-rated invoice can be issued, and there is no
default: two businesses are zero-rated for entirely different articles
and a code nobody chose is a false statement to a tax authority.

discrepancies.description: One line each, empty when it reconciles.

reconciles.description: **True is the only acceptable answer.** See below.

recovery_codes.description:
**Shown once and never again.** The server keeps only their digests, so
this list cannot be produced a second time — enrolling again is the only
way to get a new one, and it invalidates these.

code.description:
A code from the authenticator app, or one of the recovery codes.
Required when the account has a second factor — ask for it after a
`401` says so.

password.description: The new password. Twelve characters, the same floor as a signup's.

token.description:
The token from the link, **sent in the body rather than the path**: a
path lands in access logs, browser history and the `Referer` of every
asset the page loads, and this one is worth what a password is worth.

detail.description: ZATCA's words, or the first refused document and its first error.

effective_from.description:
When the business treats the registration as effective. Not a clock
reading, for the same reason a tax point is not one.

identifier.description: The number in that register — the commercial registration, usually.

industry.description:
The business's industry — `Consulting`, `Retail`, `Beauty`. It goes in
the ZATCA certificate request as the business category, so it is
required: no industry, no certificate.

name.description:
**The legal name, in Arabic** — it is what the invoice says, because the
invoice is an Arabic document.

name_latin.description: The same name in Latin script, for screens. Never sent to ZATCA.

vat_number.description: Fifteen digits, beginning and ending with `3`.

Rejected.description: One row that did not go in.

code.description: The message code, so a client can branch on it.

detail.description: What went wrong, in the language the request asked for.

row.description:
**The spreadsheet's own row number**, counting the header as row 1, so
it is the number the person's editor is showing them.

why.description: Why it came off. Kept on the record.

until.description: The end of the new term, exclusive.

reports_to.description:
Absent makes them the root. Refused if it would put somebody under
their own team.

lines.description:
The whole set, replacing what was there. Assignments are dropped: a
line that moved has to be given a unit again at its new hour.

billed_by.description:
The invoice raised for the work, once one has been —
`POST /v1/booking/reservations/{reservation}/invoice`, or the worker
when `PUT /v1/booking/billing` asks for it on completion.

secured_by.description: The payment that secured the slot, when a deposit was paid.

oneOf.description: What it came to, if it was priced.

unit.description: The unit picked out of the pool, once one has been.

example.reason: Ticket 4471: lost phone and recovery sheet, identity checked by video call.

reason.description:
Why, in 1 to 500 characters. **The only record there will be** of why
somebody's two-step sign-in was taken away: it goes into the platform
audit trail under your name, and the person themselves is told nothing
but that it happened.

email.description: The address to send a link to.

failure.description: The lender said no — a normal outcome, and the page should offer a card.

input.description:
What was paid on purchases, and the reclaimable part of it. Empty when
the tenant has no purchases module.

output.description:
What was charged on sales, net of credit notes with a tax point in this
period. Empty when the tenant has no sales module.

payable.description:
**The number that gets paid, or reclaimed.** Output tax less input tax;
negative means ZATCA owes the business.

against.description: Which line of the sale, by position from zero.

net.description:
How much of that line is coming back, excluding tax, as a positive
amount. Its tax follows from the line's own rate.

quantity.description:
**How many units are physically coming back onto the shelf**, when that
line sold stock. Optional, and never worked out from `net`: the money
and the goods are two statements. Leave it out and only the money goes
back.

serials.description:
Which units are coming back, on a line that sold serial-tracked stock —
one name per unit, as many as `quantity`, each one this sale took and
that has not come back already. Leave it out and a line of named units
can only come back whole.

branch.description:
Empty on a business with no branches, which is honest about there being
none rather than inventing a name for it.

credited.description:
Documents credited in this period. A period can show both, and the pair
is a different fact from a single net figure.

net.description: **Net of credit notes**, in minor units. What the business kept.

why.description:
Why. Kept on the record, because "which of these did we revoke after the
incident, and why" is the question afterwards.

rostered.description:
Whether a pattern has been recorded. **An empty list means "no pattern",
not "never works"** — and this is the field that stops it being read the
wrong way round.

overlap_seconds.description:
How long the old key keeps working. Omitted is seven days.

**Zero is legitimate** and means "stop now" — for a key that is known to
have leaked, where the overlap is the thing you do not want.

approved_at.description: Set once it has posted. **An approved run cannot be redrafted.**

number.description: **The statutory number**, from a gapless series. What the receipt prints.

sale.description: The `sales` invoice this became. Read it there for the lines and the QR.

ceiling_minor.description:
The most of one month's pay contributions are computed on, in minor
units. Absent means no ceiling.

configured.description:
**Whether these are the shipped defaults or something this tenant
chose.**

The shipped ones are a starting point, not an authority: GOSI's schedule
is set by the authority and has changed. This field is what tells
somebody they are still on numbers nobody has confirmed.

non_saudi_employee_bp.description:
Withheld from a non-Saudi employee. Zero: hazards cover is the
employer's alone.

saudi_employee_bp.description: Withheld from a Saudi employee's pay, in basis points.

saudi_employer_bp.description: Paid by the employer for a Saudi employee, in basis points.

name.description: What you call it. Never matched on.

rate_bp.description:
Counts earned per major unit spent, in basis points. `15_000` is a point
and a half per riyal.

link.description:
**Only after somebody else reset your two-step sign-in**: the token from
the email you were sent. A `403 auth.enrolment_link_required` means send
it. Confirming spends it.

previous.description:
**Only when replacing a factor you already have**: a code from the *old*
one, or one of its recovery codes. Replacing an enrolment destroys it
and all ten recovery codes, so it asks for proof of the thing it is
about to destroy. A `401 auth.second_factor_required` means send this
too.

Not needed for a first enrolment, which removes nothing.

required.description:
**When true, a member with no authenticator app is refused at entry.**

It refuses entry *to this tenant*: their session stays valid and their
other organisations stay reachable. Somebody already signed in is not
thrown out mid-action — they are stopped the next time they come
through the door, and told to enrol. And while it holds, a member who
has an authenticator app can replace it but not turn it off.

recovery_codes_left.description:
Recovery codes not yet spent. **Zero with `enrolled` true is a person
one lost phone away from locked out**, which is worth a warning on a
screen: enrolling again issues a fresh set.

promised.description:
**How many this call actually promised.** Fewer when the same key has
been sent before, which is what makes retrying safe.

recipients.description: How many people the audience resolved to. It can be more than one.

units.description: What it cost, in billable units. Zero on a repeat.

branch.description: Where it is. Absent in a single-branch business.

name_latin.description: For a site rendering in English. Absent means show `name`.

oneOf.description:

deposit is a fraction of. Absent for a business that bills elsewhere.

a typo is not a silently missing feature discovered at month end.

What a request produced, which is deliberately not much.

No token, and no identifier for the pending request. Both would be a way to
confirm without the mailbox, which is the whole thing this endpoint exists
to require. What comes back is what a page needs to say "check your email"
and to know when the link stops working.

Where the confirmation went. Echoed back lowercased and trimmed, which
is the form it was stored in.

items.description: What they may perform. **Empty means anything**, not nothing.

Whether the list restricts them, which is the field that stops `[]`
being read the wrong way round.

segments.description: What is billed. Equal to `messages` on every channel but SMS.

**Standard invoices not yet cleared.** Not late — a standard invoice is
cleared before issue — but documents the buyer must not have yet.

How many documents are in each state: `unregistered`, `pending`,
`cleared`, `reported`, `refused`.

**Simplified invoices past their 24 hours and still not reported.** The
number an inspection asks about.

Whether there is a registration at all. Nothing can be cleared or
reported without one, so everything else here is moot until it is true.

**Documents with no signature yet.** They can be neither submitted nor
printed with a phase-two QR, so this is the number that says a business
is not really live whatever else is true.

What a delivery owes before anybody has billed for it — a liability.
Defaults to 2010. A receipt credits it; the supplier's bill line that
names the product debits it back.

What a write-off threw away. Defaults to 5900 as well — they are two
fields so a business that wants spoilage apart from shrinkage can have
it without a code change, not because the shipped charts separate them.

**What the shelf owes**: what the units no lot could cover were charged
out at, less what returns and counts have settled. A delivery since does
not pay it; a count does. Absent while nothing has ever been received
onto the shelf.

days.description:
How many days ahead of an expiry the business wants warning. Nothing to
ten years.

One per branch with a shelf, the shelves of no branch first. Empty when
nothing has been received or sold.

The last day `expiring` reaches: `today` plus the tenant's expiry
window.

The tenant's day the dates below were read against, on its own
calendar.

branch.description: Absent on a business that sends no `X-Branch`.

The product's name, as declared. `null` only when the read model holds
no declaration for it: the row is still listed.

The open lots added up, **less what the shelf owes**. Negative when a
plain product has been sold off an empty shelf — a till does not stop
for a bad count (R1), and the negative number is the report a count
corrects.

What that is carried at: the sum of the lots' own values, less what any
units sold short were charged out at, and never an average across them.
Absent until something has been received here.

Exclusive, and it **moves**: resuming pushes it out by exactly the time
the clock was stopped for.

Why, in 1 to 500 characters. **Written for the tenant's owner**, not
as an internal note: they read it in their tenant's audit trail.

Cash out that was not a refund — a banking run, a float moved, a
supplier paid in notes. The closest the log comes to "what was banked",
and named for what it is: nothing here has seen a bank statement.

Shifts this operator **closed**. A till still taking money has no
variance yet.

**What the drawer disagreed by**, summed over the shifts this operator
closed. Negative is short.

none**: how much dearer is the one number a business must choose for
itself, and a preset would be choosing it for them.

resources.description:
